_comment: Identity policy for the role that runs `terraform apply`. It is NEVER given to the
agent: it is assumed out of band, by CI on a human-approved plan, or by an operator
with MFA. See deploy-role-trust-policy.json for who may assume it.
Terraform needs iam:CreateRole to build a pipeline -- a Glue job needs an execution
role -- and anything holding CreateRole plus AttachRolePolicy can mint an admin role and
use it. There is no least-privilege Terraform role that can still create IAM. The answer
is not to withhold CreateRole; it is to CAP what gets created:
1. Every role this creates must carry MinusOpsAppPermissionsBoundary. Enforced by an
iam:PermissionsBoundary condition, so a create without it is denied.
2. Role management is confined to the /minusops-managed/ path, so platform roles --
including this one and the plan role -- are out of reach.
3. The boundary policy itself cannot be edited or detached. A boundary the bounded
principal can rewrite is decoration.
4. iam:PassRole is scoped by iam:PassedToService. Unscoped, an agent passes an admin
role to a Lambda it controls and inherits that role's authority without ever
holding a destructive permission itself.
The service list is derived from what modules/*/main.tf actually provisions (76 aws_*
resource types across 29 modules), not from a general-purpose data-platform allowance.
Extend it when a module introduces a new service; do not pre-grant.
Replace <ACCOUNT_ID>, <STATE_BUCKET>, <LOCK_TABLE>, <STATE_KEY_ID>.
Resource is * because Terraform names resources at apply time and cannot be
pre-enumerated. The bound is the ACTION set, plus the SCP that denies the
irreversible subset above any policy in this account.
The escalation cap. A create or a policy attach without the boundary ARN is denied,
so every role Terraform mints is capped by the same ceiling this role is.
Lifecycle operations that cannot escalate. Confined to the same path, so this role
cannot touch the plan role, this role, or any platform role.
Unscoped iam:PassRole is the escalation people miss. With Resource "*" an agent
hands an admin role to a Lambda it just created, invokes it, and inherits that
role's authority -- without ever holding a destructive permission itself.

Statement._comment: A boundary the bounded principal can detach is not a boundary.

_comment: Editing the boundary lifts the ceiling. Scoped to the boundary ARN, deliberately:
a blanket deny on iam:DeletePolicyVersion breaks every managed-policy update once
the 5-version quota is reached, including ones this role legitimately makes.
The path condition above already confines writes, but this makes the intent
explicit and survives someone widening that Resource by mistake.
